title: Choose Righton's visual world
question: Every option keeps your two pins: the deep-green glow background and the Afriwork page structure. They differ in the idea the page is built around. Keep the roll, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Three Rounds
options.lineage: the Ethiopian coffee ceremony's three pours: Abol, Tona, Bereka
options.thesis: Hiring through Righton as a hosted ritual in three rounds: you apply, Righton screens and introduces, the client hires.
materials: a single roasted-copper ink reserved for Apply
options.viewport: Afriwork structure on the green glow: announcement bar (Telegram), nav, centred headline with Find work / Hire through Righton, and under it a live sample vacancy (Ref RT-0142, closes in 12 days) whose three round markers fill in sequence.
options.risk: If the ritual is taken too literally (cups, pots, beans) it reads folkloric instead of professional. It has to live in the structure and numbering, not in illustrations.

raised.raise: Every vacancy carries a reference number (RT-0142) that can be typed straight into search, the way teletext pages are keyed by number.
One action colour, roasted copper, is reserved for Apply alone. Everything else is green and white.
Every listing is labelled with the date posted and a countdown in days to its deadline, like a dated jar label.

options.label: Vacancy Announcement
options.lineage: the boxed vacancy notices in The Reporter and Addis Zemen classifieds
options.thesis: Every opening typeset as the vacancy notice every Ethiopian job seeker already knows how to read.
materials: crisp white notice cards with ruled fields
options.viewport: Afriwork structure on the green glow: centred headline and two actions, with a fanned stack of three typeset vacancy notices rising from the arc (Position, Ref No., Qualification, Experience, Salary, Deadline).
options.risk: Also the direction most runs would land on, and it's the closest to a print classifieds page. It's familiar, which is both its strength and its ceiling.

options.label: Teletext Service
options.thesis: Vacancies as numbered broadcast pages on a black grid.
options.viewport: A P100 index page listing vacancies as numbered rows.
options.risk: Fights the pinned green glow and the request for a sleek, professional look.
options.case: Loses on both axes: job seekers in Addis don't recognise teletext, and it contradicts the pinned background.
options.kept: Jobs addressed by a typeable reference number.

options.label: Creator Hardware Bench
options.lineage: desk instruments with keycaps and one orange key
options.thesis: The portal as a tactile instrument with one orange action key.
options.viewport: A keycap grid of job categories with an orange Apply key.
options.risk: A gadget aesthetic that clashes with the pinned green glow.
options.case: Loses on both axes: the audience doesn't identify with it, and it says nothing about recruiting.
options.kept: A single colour reserved for the one action that matters.

options.label: Brine Calendar
options.lineage: seasonal pickling jars with dated labels
options.thesis: Openings as dated jars maturing on a shelf.
options.viewport: A shelf of labelled vacancy jars.
options.risk: Playful and food-coded, the opposite of the professional brief.
options.case: Loses on both axes: off-subject, and it softens trust.
options.kept: Every item banded with its dates and a day count.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Afriwork's structure on your green glow, played straight and executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Announcement bar, nav, big two-line headline with two pill buttons, floating chips and a sector strip in place of employer logos.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other job board by design.
